clue.text: One who is what he eats?

definitions.text: One who is what he eats?

parts.words: One who is what he eats?
parts.note: plays on the saying 'you are what you eat': someone who dines on fellow humans is literally made of the same stuff as the meal

explanation.surface: A diet philosopher's riddle about becoming one's food.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'you are what you eat' is turned literal: a person whose food is other people is what they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh is, in a grim literal sense, the same species as the dinner.

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone tells an impersonating officer that the act is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic is an imitator, one who reproduces what others do, just as a photocopying machine duplicates pages.

indicators.note: rowdy means disorderly and unruly, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A claim that noisy lionesses have gone quiet, an obvious contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hushed makes no sound at all, i.e. it is silent.

clue.text: Feed from tin ordered by hungry wimp

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of 'tin' are put in a different order

parts.note: ravenous means extremely hungry
a drip is a feeble, wet person, a wimp

explanation.surface: A weakling who is starving orders a meal straight from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges TIN into INT; 'from' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital line delivering fluids and nutrients directly into a vein is a way of feeding a patient.

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a line of verse is an example of a lyric, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a lyric from the song Rule, Britannia.
explanation.walkthrough: Britannia Airways was a British charter carrier, so 'Britannia' is the definition, not the patriotic song.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia Airways was a British holiday carrier, a company flying passengers.

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of 'A vicar' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman cooks scrambled eggs for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' looks like the cooking method but rearranges A VICAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe served as a delicacy consists of fish eggs.

clue.text: Drugs article by current media workers

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tide is a current of the sea
the press is the news media
ants are the classic crossword workers, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A report on drugs written by journalists in today's media.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines that lift low mood are a class of drugs.

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the gold sits inside the climbing plant

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A mountaineer carrying gold and wearing white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer but is the plant IVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant-tusk colour is a creamy shade of white.

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, here losing the first letter

parts.note: George Bush was a US president

explanation.surface: A bush is cut back so that a trainee can do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like a shrub, hence 'pruned', but it is the former US President.
explanation.definitionFit: In US hospitals a junior doctor in training, an intern, is also called a house officer or resident.

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the next

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state Georgia
end means death

explanation.surface: A death sentence scheduled in one US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is its schedule.

clue.text: Indicate glass with nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the glass just named

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at an empty glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'nothing' does not mean the glass is empty but gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to show or direct attention to it with a finger.

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange for the houris of paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Houris are the beautiful maidens of paradise in Islamic tradition; 'organised' rearranges GET HOURIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and morally upright are synonyms.

indicators.note: negotiated means worked out or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A local man born under Leo bargains for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges NATIVE LEO; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting something up, a raise, is an elevation.

parts.note: dry means dull and uninteresting
AD (Anno Domini) marks the present era

explanation.surface: A boring contemporary person living in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a wood nymph lives in trees, a forest-dweller.

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RE, religious education, stands for theology
ever means always

explanation.surface: Worship is always part of the study of theology.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship is to venerate or adore deeply.

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: aspiring means longing for, craving

explanation.surface: An addict endlessly craving a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkiller, acetylsalicylic acid, is a drug.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer
to sing is underworld slang for to confess to police

explanation.surface: Forcing a soldier and a boxer to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: Realising a profit or ambition means achieving or making it happen.

parts.note: vessels suggests ships but means blood vessels carrying blood from the heart, work vital to life

explanation.surface: Ships performing essential duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood vessels carrying oxygenated blood from the heart keep the body alive.

parts.note: a rest is a break
ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: A choice between repairing and smashing rock.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something broken is to repair it to its former state.

clue.text: One who may chop and change?

definitions.text: One who may chop and change?

parts.words: One who may chop and change?
parts.note: the idiom about being fickle is read literally: someone who cuts and alters text for publication

explanation.surface: A fickle person who keeps changing their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who cuts and revises copy for a publication does this job.

indicators.note: invention means something newly made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy woman came up with an invention.
explanation.walkthrough: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Dionysus.
explanation.definitionFit: A frenzied female devotee of Bacchus is a wild madwoman.

indicators.note: puncturing means piercing into, so the joke goes inside the other piece

parts.note: may and might are both modal verbs of possibility
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A joke deflating power and pomp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a noun meaning power, but as a verb it gives MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal grandeur or stateliness is the sense of royal dignity.

definitions.meaning: a failing is a flaw or shortcoming
to desert one's country or party for the opposition

explanation.definitionFit: A fault or flaw is the noun sense; to desert to the other camp is the verb sense.

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening letter

parts.note: leaves are pages of a book

explanation.surface: Uncut book pages that stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower edge of a roof projecting beyond the walls is its overhang.

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of vile

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A rather nasty government transport minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' suggests a government post but means a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish clergyman is a minister of the church.

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
just means only
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Disapproval of someone dressed in nothing but jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfair act, a wrong, is an act of unfairness.

parts.note: to incur debts is to run them up
IOUs are written promises to pay, debts

explanation.surface: Borrowing money at zero interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without interest' suggests an interest-free loan but means lacking curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking curiosity shows no interest in things.

clue.text: Artless Italian in part of church

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated Italian standing in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means innocent and unworldly, without guile.

parts.note: a strip, or striptease, is a performance that reveals the body

explanation.surface: An English band puts on a show baring all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians but means a stripe of colour; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strip of contrasting colour is a band.

indicators.note: in means placed inside the number

parts.note: the numeral is read as the word for the number, not as a reference to 8-down
yes is agreement, not contradicting

explanation.surface: A logic puzzle about a statement with no contradiction making sense.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a cross-reference to 8-down but is simply the number EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses.
